title: Bread at Rosespire
aim: The listener wonders what was made.
lines: Rosespire has made bread.
From wheat?
Yes.

title: A rumour of bread
aim: The listener asks what kind of bread was heard about.
lines: People say Rosespire has made bread from wheat.
I wonder what the bread is like.

title: The uncertain oven
aim: The listener responds to a faint piece of news.
lines: Rosespire may have made bread from wheat.
I wonder what it tastes like.

title: Quillen at Silverwick
aim: The listener asks what brought Quillen to the company.
lines: Quillen Barrowward joined the Unpaid Company after looking for food at Silverwick.
For long?
Days.
A long wait for a meal.

title: Alda in the Tallow Knives
aim: The listener asks about Alda's reason for joining.
lines: People say Alda Millrace joined the Tallow Knives after looking for food at Gloamgate.
Was Alda looking long?
Days, from what I hear.
I hope there was a meal at the end of it.

title: Reida, perhaps
aim: The listener asks what Reida was seeking.
lines: Reida Millrace may have joined the Tallow Knives after looking for food at Gloamgate.
Do you know how Reida got on?
I’d have to ask.

title: Two places in the herd
aim: The listener checks the difference between a new calf and an older working calf.
lines: Rosespire's herd raised a new calf, and an older calf joined the working herd.
The new one is still growing?
Yes. The older one joined the workers.
That is good news for the herd.

title: Silverwick's calves
aim: The listener asks which calf joined the working herd.
lines: People say Silverwick has a new calf, and an older calf joined the working herd.
Which one joined the workers?
The older calf.
I wonder what the new one looks like.

title: A doubtful calving report
aim: The listener responds to an uncertain calf report.
lines: Silverwick may have a new calf, and an older calf may have joined the working herd.
I wonder what the new calf looks like.
I do too.

title: Fodder ran short
aim: The listener asks why the cattle were slaughtered.
lines: Rosespire slaughtered cattle when the fodder ran short. The beef went into the local store.
Will the rest have enough feed?
That’s worth asking.

title: Alderwatch's cattle
aim: The listener asks what led to the beef in the store.
lines: I hear Alderwatch slaughtered cattle after fodder ran short.
What happened to the meat?
It went into the local store as beef, from what I hear.

title: A story of cattle
aim: The listener responds to an uncertain loss.
lines: Rosespire may have slaughtered cattle after fodder ran short.
Short of feed?
That’s the story. The beef went into the local store, if it’s true.

title: The goblin Keeper
aim: The listener asks what title the goblin earned.
lines: A goblin rose to Keeper in the dragon cult through service.
Keeper?
Yes. That is the title.
Good for them.

title: The Bearer report
aim: The listener asks what role the goblin took.
lines: People say a goblin rose to Bearer in the dragon cult through service.
Bearer of what?
I do not know.
The title still sounds busy.

title: An uncertain promotion
aim: The listener asks what role may have been earned.
lines: A goblin may have risen to Bearer in the dragon cult through service.
Bearer?
That is the word I heard.
I wonder what they carry.

title: Othwen's life in Hollowbarrow
aim: The listener responds to news of Othwen's death.
lines: Othwen Herald has died.
Where did Othwen live?
Hollowbarrow.
I’m sorry to hear it.

title: Rodric Bowyer's death
aim: The listener responds to retold news of a death.
lines: I hear Rodric Bowyer has died.
Rodric lived in Hollowbarrow?
Yes, from what people say.
Sad news.

title: Uncertain news of Rodric
aim: The listener hears an uncertain report about a local death.
lines: Rodric Bowyer may have died after a life in Hollowbarrow.
I hope someone knows for sure.

title: Crowns for grain
aim: The listener asks about a grain purchase without assuming delivery.
lines: Indigo March has put money into Hollowbarrow’s market to buy grain.
Has the grain arrived?
I’ve only heard about the money so far.

title: A grain purchase retold
aim: The listener takes an interest in a retold market decision.
lines: People say Indigo March has sent money to Hollowbarrow’s market for grain.
How soon might the grain come?
I’d like to know that myself.

title: The Covenant's grain money
aim: The listener asks what an uncertain funding report might change.
lines: Silver Covenant may have sent money to Hollowbarrow’s market to buy grain.
Grain for Hollowbarrow?
That seems to be the plan, if the story is right.

title: Gloamgate burned
aim: The listener asks about the stated cause of a dragon's fire.
lines: Varkesh the Unappeased burned Gloamgate.
What brought that on?
Stolen crowns were still missing.
What a terrible price for the town.

title: The fire retold
aim: The listener asks a particular question about a retold dragon attack.
lines: I hear Varkesh the Unappeased burned Gloamgate over stolen crowns that were still missing.
Did anyone find the crowns afterward?
I haven’t heard that part.

title: A fire story
aim: The listener reacts to an uncertain report of a dragon's motive.
lines: Varkesh the Unappeased may have burned Gloamgate over missing stolen crowns.
Who took them?
I only heard that they were missing.

title: Smoke in the chimneys
aim: The listener asks about a prophecy while it remains a prediction.
lines: Smoke is falling into Gloamgate’s chimneys.
What do the old readers make of it?
They say Varkesh the Unappeased will come before long.
I wonder what they see in the smoke.

title: Nights counted
aim: The listener responds to a retold omen with practical concern.
lines: People say smoke is falling into Gloamgate’s chimneys. The old readers expect Varkesh the Unappeased before long.
What would you make of that?
I’d be uneasy.

title: An uncertain omen
aim: The listener asks about an uncertain prophecy without making it certain.
lines: There may be smoke falling into Gloamgate’s chimneys. They say the old readers are counting the nights until Varkesh the Unappeased comes.
I wonder how they read the smoke.

title: Mutton at Rosespire
aim: The listener asks about the practical result of a flock cull.
lines: Rosespire slaughtered sheep after winter fodder ran short.
What happened to the meat?
The mutton went into the local store.

title: Fodder and mutton
aim: The listener takes an interest in retold food news.
lines: I hear Rosespire slaughtered sheep after winter fodder ran short, then stored the mutton locally.
Will the flock have enough feed now?
I haven’t heard.

title: Alderwatch's mutton
aim: The listener responds to an uncertain report about local food.
lines: Alderwatch may have slaughtered sheep after winter fodder ran short.
Was the meat kept?
Mutton went into the local store, if the story is true.

title: The Cinder Tithe at Gloamgate
aim: The listener asks about an alleged raid while the treasure stays unnamed.
lines: The Cinder Tithe raided Gloamgate.
What did they take?
Bread, crowns, and a treasure.
Which treasure?
That part hasn’t reached me.

title: A raid at Rosespire
aim: The listener asks about retold losses from a raid.
lines: People say the Cinder Tithe raided Rosespire and took bread and crowns.
How is the town managing?
I’d like to know.

title: Wheat taken at Thornford
aim: The listener checks what the raiders took.
lines: There’s talk of the Cinder Tithe raiding Thornford for wheat.
Crowns as well?
The account says they took none.
I wonder what happened to the wheat.

title: Grain for the east
aim: The listener asks which settlements the short harvest affects.
lines: Thornford’s drought harvest fell short.
Who was it meant to feed?
The settlements to the east.
That’s hard news for them.

title: Grain for the south
aim: The listener wonders how the shortfall could be met.
lines: I hear Thornford’s harvest is too small to supply the southern settlements.
Could they get grain elsewhere?
I’d have to ask.

title: An uncertain harvest
aim: The listener asks which direction the reported shortage affects.
lines: Thornford may have too little grain for the settlements it supplies.
Which ones?
Those to the south, from what I heard.

title: A new pony
aim: The listener responds to a new foal.
lines: Gloamgate has raised a pony foal, and a pony has joined the working herd.
I’d like to see the foal.
So would I.

title: Ponies at Alderwatch
aim: The listener asks about an account of pony breeding.
lines: There’s word of a new pony foal at Alderwatch.
Has their working herd grown too?
A pony has joined it, I hear.

title: A foal at Thornford
aim: The listener takes an interest in an uncertain birth report.
lines: Someone’s saying Thornford has a new pony foal.
A little pony?
That’s what I heard. I’d like to see it myself.

title: Lambs and yearlings
aim: The listener distinguishes new lambs from the older animals.
lines: Rosespire has new lambs, and yearlings have joined the adult flock.
The yearlings are the older ones?
Yes. The lambs still have their growing to do.

title: A growing flock
aim: The listener asks about the older sheep.
lines: I hear Alderwatch has raised lambs.
And the yearlings?
They’ve joined the adult flock, from what I hear.
Good to hear they’re growing.

title: News of lambs
aim: The listener seeks a detail beyond the doubtful account.
lines: There may be new lambs at Alderwatch. Some yearlings have joined the adult flock too, if the story is right.
What are the lambs like?
I only heard about them.

title: Masonry at Hollowbarrow
aim: The listener asks about the repair material.
lines: Hollowbarrow’s masons have repaired public buildings.
With stone?
Yes.
I’d like to see the work.

title: Repairs on hold
aim: The listener finds out why repairs are delayed.
lines: Gloamgate’s public repairs are waiting, I hear.
For workers?
For stone, from what people say.
They’ll need something to build with.

title: Repairs at Silverwick
aim: The listener asks where the reported work took place.
lines: Silverwick’s masons may have done some repairs with stone.
On the public buildings?
That’s the report.

title: Making paper
aim: The listener asks what went into the paper.
lines: Rosespire’s mill has made paper.
From what?
Wood.
That must be interesting to watch.

title: Paper at Gloamgate
aim: The listener wonders about the paper’s eventual use.
lines: They say Gloamgate’s mill has made paper from wood.
I wonder what will be written on it.

title: A rumour of paper
aim: The listener asks about a doubtful production report.
lines: There’s a rumour that Gloamgate’s mill has made paper.
From wood?
That’s what I heard.
